subject: Re: Northbound Health — proposal for exit schedule & capped penalties
messages:
From: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@northboundhealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@northboundhealth.com>, procurement@northboundhealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA remedies — request for capped buyout + liquidated damages clause

Sofia / Ben —

Thanks for the call this morning. As discussed, Northbound has experienced three P1 latency incidents in the last 45 days, two of which caused visible degradation in our clinician-facing workflows. Our execs are escalating and procurement is asking for contractual remedies beyond recurring credits. Specifically they want:

- A 90-day cure window after an initial P1 and a right to terminate for convenience if the same customer experiences 2 additional P1s within a 90-day rolling window;
- A capped buyout (fee-at-risk) option tied to a sliding scale based on severity and recurrence (not just credits);
- A liquidated damages alternative if outages are prolonged beyond 48 hours and remediation has not restored service to the agreed latency profile.

We appreciate the performance optimization work you outlined, but procurement needs concrete contract language to satisfy their board. Please send a concrete counterproposal with numbers and timeline by next week.

Attachments: incident-summary-Nov2026.pdf (redacted), request-matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Aaron
VP Engineering — Northbound Health
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@northboundhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA remedies — request for capped buyout + liquidated damages clause

Aaron —

Really sorry to hear about the impact on your clinicians. We take reliability seriously and want to find a path that addresses Northbound’s risk appetite while keeping the contract operationally reasonable. High-level counterproposal below; legal will follow with precise language.

1) Escalation + cure: we can accept a 90-day monitored cure period after a P1. During that period, we will prioritize dedicated routing and increased capacity for your tenant at no additional cost.

2) Staged buyout (conditional, capped): instead of an immediate liquidated damages regime, we propose a staged buyout option that becomes available after recurrence thresholds:
   - After 2 P1s within 90 days: customer may elect a partial buyout equal to 25% of 3 months’ committed spend for the affected service, payable within 60 days of election.
   - After 4 P1s within 180 days: customer may elect full buyout equal to 100% of 3 months’ committed spend, payable within 30 days.
   - Aggregate cap: buyout payments capped at 3x monthly committed spend in any 12-month period.

3) Extended outage remedy: for outages exceeding 48 consecutive hours where our mitigation fails to restore the platform to the agreed availability range, we can add an alternative remedy pathway: an additional one-time cash payment equal to 50% of one month’s committed spend, but only where the outage is directly attributable to Redwood and not to customer misconfiguration or force majeure.

4) Operational precondition: before any buyout/termination becomes effective, we require:
   - Completed post-incident RCA and acceptance of remediation plan;
   - Reasonable attempt at operational fixes (KV cache warm, regional failover exercised);
   - Mutually agreed timeline for migration or handover if termination is exercised.

We believe this approach balances accountability and predictability: you get a meaningful financial remedy that scales with recurrence while keeping the runway for a joint remediation path. Marissa (legal) is drafting formal language and I’ll loop Connor on the runbook updates.

Can you confirm whether the proposed numeric caps are in the ballpark for procurement? If not, tell us target bounds and we’ll iterate.

Best,
Sofia
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@northboundhealth.com>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA remedies — request for capped buyout + liquidated damages clause

Aaron / team —

Quick legal note: the structure Sofia proposes is intended to be implementable without creating an open-ended liability exposure. Key points to flag in drafting:

- Define P1 precisely (latency/service degradation thresholds, monitoring windows).
- Carve out customer misconfigurations, third-party cloud incidents, and force majeure from buyout triggers.
- Include a mutual remediation cooperation clause and a defined RCA acceptance process (timeline: 14 days after incident closure).
- Cap aggregate exposure (we propose 3x monthly committed spend) and tie any cash payments to an agreed invoice schedule.
- For the 48-hour extended outage clause, we propose a strict causal showing that Redwood’s platform caused the outage; otherwise we risk paying for infra outside our control.

I’ve attached a redline with suggested language and a short-runbook template to satisfy operational preconditions. Happy to hop on a call if you want to walk through line-by-line.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel — Redwood Inference
From: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@northboundhealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@northboundhealth.com, elena.park@northboundhealth.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA remedies — request for capped buyout + liquidated damages clause

Sofia / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the concrete numbers. Procurement reviewed and provided feedback:

- They want the buyout scale to be more front-loaded for repeat incidents. Suggested: 40% after 2 P1s in 90 days, 100% after 3 P1s in 180 days.
- Aggregate cap at 6x monthly committed spend (procurement insists on a higher cap).
- For the 48-hour clause, they prefer a liquidated damages schedule of 5% of monthly committed spend per 24-hour period beyond 48 hours, up to a max of 50% of one month’s committed spend.

They are willing to accept the operational preconditions and an RCA process, but procurement needs the financials to be explicit in the MSA. Aaron

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@northboundhealth.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Northbound Health — proposal for exit schedule & capped penalties

Team —

Thanks for the procurement feedback, Aaron. We can accommodate a refined commercial counterproposal but need to protect against runaway exposure and ensure the remedies remain proportional. Proposed revisions for your internal review (we can table these for contract markup):

- After 2 P1s in 90 days: buyout = 35% of 3 months’ committed spend (middle ground).
- After 3 P1s in 180 days: buyout = 100% of 3 months’ committed spend.
- Aggregate cap: 4x monthly committed spend in any 12-month period.
- Liquidated damages for extended outage: 2.5% of monthly committed spend per 24-hour period beyond 48 hours, capped at 25% of one month’s committed spend — payable only where outage is demonstrably attributable to Redwood and not excluded causes.

Operational guardrails we insist on: documented RCAs within 14 days, a 30-day remediation runway post-RCA before termination for convenience converts to an orderly migration assistance period, and a mutual cooperation clause for data extraction.

I’ll attach a clean commercial term sheet with these revised numbers and ask Marissa to produce a redline MSA for your counsel. Ben / Connor — please prepare a short migration/runbook offer (30/60/90 day options) we can include if termination is exercised. Aaron — if you can confirm this is within procurement’s stretch tolerances, we’ll move to contractual markup tomorrow.

Best,
Sofia
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: NBH_Commercial_Termsheet_v2.pdf
